description.p: Apsis takes rsync snapshots of your system onto a backup disk, lists them and deletes them. It lives in the COSMIC panel, where it shows when the last snapshot was taken and how full the backup disk is, and opens a window laid out like Timeshift's: a toolbar, the snapshot list, and a status area with the progress of a running snapshot.

ul.li: Snapshots with rsync: later ones only copy what changed and hard-link the rest, at idle I/O priority
Choose whether /root and /home go into a snapshot; the system always does
A filter list to leave out or keep folders, files and patterns
Delete one snapshot or several; stop a snapshot while it's being made
A reminder when the last snapshot is old, and a warning when the backup disk is nearly full
One password prompt per few minutes, through a small polkit-guarded helper

description.p: Snapshots use Timeshift's on-disk layout, so snapshots Timeshift made keep working, but Apsis doesn't need or run Timeshift. Manual only: there is no schedule, and snapshots are only deleted when you delete them. Restoring the whole system is experimental (Pop!_OS 24.04 with systemd-boot); encrypted (LUKS) backup disks aren't supported.

description.p: A copied disk label can't stand in for the backup disk.

ul.li: When two devices carry the backup disk's filesystem UUID, Apsis uses neither and names both
A restore waiting for its restart refuses the same way, with nothing changed

description.p: A snapshot's progress only goes forward.

ul.li: The percent no longer jumps back and forth, and a snapshot no longer ends at a few percent; it keeps moving through large unchanged parts of the system
Until rsync has listed every file, the progress says "scanning files"; the time left shows only once it means something
The panel popup is a status line over the window's bar: the backup disk's use, or the snapshot's progress while one runs

description.p: The panel popup is a ring.

ul.li: The ring shows how full the backup disk is, with the age of the last snapshot in its centre; while a snapshot or a restore's preparation runs, it shows the progress
The age turns the warning colour when a snapshot is overdue, and the ring when the disk is nearly full
The popup no longer lists snapshots or shows success messages; the window has both

description.p: Restore now works on an encrypted Pop!_OS install: an LVM volume inside one LUKS partition, the layout Pop!_OS's installer makes with "Encrypt drive". Restore stays experimental, for Pop!_OS 24.04 with systemd-boot.

ul.li: Restore on an encrypted system disk; the passphrase is asked twice, at the restart that runs the restore and at the start after it
A check that the new boot files can still unlock the disk; if they can't, the computer keeps the boot files it had
The recovery note on the backup disk starts with the lines that unlock the disk
Only the "Encrypt drive" layout: LUKS without LVM, and LVM without LUKS, are refused before anything happens
A snapshot made while Apsis 0.5.x was installed puts 0.5.x back; on an encrypted system, install 0.6.0 again after such a restore

description.p: Restoring the whole system to a snapshot, at the next start. Experimental; Pop!_OS 24.04 with systemd-boot only.

ul.li: Restore checks that the snapshot fits this computer, takes a safety snapshot first (on by default) and asks once more at "Ready to restore"
The restore runs at the next start with the desktop stopped, and keeps the old boot files if the refresh or the check fails
A recovery note with this machine's UUIDs is written on the backup disk
Upgrading, reinstalling or removing the package is refused while a job runs (not when upgrading from 0.4.x: the old package's script doesn't wait)
A delete cut off part-way leaves a dimmed row that Delete removes

description.p: Deleting several snapshots works again with more than one display.

ul.li: Several snapshots are deleted as one job; the password is asked once
Lists share the backup disk and never refuse each other
Snapshots and deletes wait for lists to finish instead of being refused

description.p: Snapshots now hold everything a full restore needs.

ul.li: Snapshots keep POSIX ACLs and extended attributes, including file capabilities
Older snapshots, and Timeshift's, keep working
The first snapshot after the upgrade copies a few files again; later ones link as before

description.p: A window laid out like Timeshift's, and a simpler Apsis.

ul.li: New window: a toolbar (Create, Delete, Settings), the snapshot list, and a status area
Settings as tabs: Location, Include (/root, /home), Filters, Misc
Stop a snapshot while it's being made
Every window and the panel popup show a snapshot being made elsewhere
Leftovers of an interrupted snapshot are removed by the next one, or with Delete
A backup disk pulled out during a snapshot is named as such
Removed: restoring single files, keep last N, per-user home folder modes
Opening Apsis again brings the open window forward instead of opening another
A window opened while a snapshot job runs says it is busy and waits for the job
The backup disk being unplugged or plugged in shows without refreshing
A create that loses its disk says so plainly; the raw error goes to the log
The create room shows whether your home folder is included
The file browser says when a home folder was not included in a snapshot
After a restore to a folder, Apsis says where the files went and can open it

description.p: A cleaner look and a status you can read at a glance.

ul.li: The panel popup is a read-only overview: last snapshot, backup disk bar, newest snapshots
The window has four rooms: snapshots, create, schedule and log, with an apsis strip on top
The panel tooltip shows last, next and disk; the icon and an optional panel label show the state
The disk bar turns to the warning and critical colours when space runs low
Progress with the time left while a snapshot is created or restored
Every colour now comes from the COSMIC theme
A clearer message for a leftover from an interrupted snapshot

description.p: Apsis is standalone: it takes rsync snapshots itself and no longer needs Timeshift.

ul.li: Snapshots, delete and file restore without Timeshift; existing Timeshift snapshots keep working
Its own settings in /etc/apsis/config.toml, imported once from Timeshift's settings
rsync runs at idle I/O priority
Keep the last N snapshots (preview, then confirm) and a reminder when the last snapshot is old
A bar of the backup disk's free space, and progress with the time left
Removed: Timeshift's schedule and mode settings
Upgrading: open the settings once and press w to import
Delete several snapshots at once: mark them with space or J, then press d
Delete prompts and results show the date and comment instead of the raw name
Right-click menu: Close, and Remove or move applet
A manual page (man apsis) and a settings guide in the README
The settings explanations are no longer cut off
A .deb package for Pop!_OS and Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, attached to each release
A "How to use" guide in the README
Fixed: just vendor now writes vendor.tar, and just build-vendored builds offline
List, create and delete Timeshift snapshots from a COSMIC panel applet
Terminal-style popup and window mode, keyboard and mouse
Timeshift settings view
apsis-helper: a D-Bus service guarded by polkit
Experimental native rsync backend and file-level restore
